documented_baselines.methodology: Count each competitor_steps array entry once, without splitting combined steps or summing overlapping/alternative routes. These are documentation bullets, not operator actions or authenticated transactions.

flows.name: 06 — Import loose skill files
steps: New skill → Import skills → Upload.
Select files containing SKILL.md and supporting resources.
Review detected skills and import statuses; select the intended subset.
Import creates versions for changes, marks identical content Already up to date and preserves existing production labels.

flows.name: 07 — Import folders and multi-skill ZIP archives
steps: New skill → Import skills → Upload and choose a folder or ZIP.
Review discovered SKILL.md roots and file counts; search/select the skills to import.
Confirm changed/new packages and skip Already up to date entries.
Respect the documented 3 MiB compressed ZIP limit and per-version limits of 200 files and 1,000,000 UTF-8 bytes.

flows.name: 20 — Push a local skill from the CLI
steps: Install @langfuse/cli and configure project credentials/host.
Run langfuse skills push <folder> --dry-run --json to inspect included/excluded paths.
Add literal --exclude paths as needed; review tracked files because ignore rules do not exclude already-tracked files.
Push with an optional commit message and explicit label.
Matching latest files reuse the version; Git inspection failure stops publication.

flows.name: 21 — Recursively push a repository's skill collection
steps: Run skills push <directory> --recursive.
Use --update-only to restrict the operation to existing skills when desired.
Inspect --dry-run --json output and per-skill exclusions.
Optionally use --no-lockfile, then perform the push.

flows.name: 22 — Install a skill, pinned version, tag or complete project catalog
steps: Use skill → Install with CLI → Configure install command.
Choose one skill, a tag or all project skills; choose a label/version and installation directory.
Copy/run skills install <name>, <name>@staging, <name>@3, --tag or --all.
Default output is .agents/skills/<name>; configure the agent to read it.

flows.name: 23 — Restore from lock, update followers and preserve pins
steps: Keep langfuse-skills.lock from installation.
Run skills install with no arguments to restore locked versions.
Run skills update to refresh already-locked label followers; exact pins stay fixed.
Re-run install --tag or --all to discover newly added skills.
The CLI rejects manifests inconsistent with requested selectors; --force does not bypass that validation.

flows.name: PromptLayer Skill Collections — author/import a multi-skill context folder
steps: Create/edit a Skill Collection or ask Wrangler to create one.
Choose Claude Code, OpenAI/Codex, OpenClaw or Universal layout.
Add skill subfolders, provider core files and supporting files.
Import folders or ZIPs; the changelog also documents binary-file upload/preview.
Edit links/frontmatter, review the file/provider diff and save with a commit message.
Use version history to compare or restore and labels to mark the intended release.

flows.name: PromptLayer Skill Collections — pull via SDK/REST and author via MCP/API
steps: Open Pull via SDK to generate collection-specific instructions.
Set the API key in the environment and call client.skills.pull by collection identifier.
Choose latest, exact version or release label; request a file map or ZIP.
Write/extract files to the intended project layout.
Use GET /api/public/v2/skill-collections/{identifier} for REST retrieval.
Save new versions through JSON file_updates/moves/deletes or multipart ZIP; MCP exposes list/create/get/update/save-version tools.

flows.name: Reconcile Git/project context with Hub edits during deployment
steps: Modify instructions.md or skills locally, or edit those files in Context Hub after the last deploy.
Run mda deploy; if Hub changed since last sync, interactive CLI asks whether to overwrite, defaulting to keeping Hub and skipping that section.
In noninteractive CI, conflict causes an error until rerun with --context-strategy overwrite or --context-strategy keep-hub.
Overwrite replaces the changed section from project files; keep-hub skips syncing it. A concurrent change during sync causes a commit conflict and requires another deploy.

flows.name: Remove stale deployed skills and apply Hub-only hotfixes
steps: For a lasting removal, delete the local skill files and run mda deploy; deploy removes previously deployed skill files that no longer exist locally.
For a quick change, open deployment Details → Context Hub and edit instructions or skills.
The Hub edit can apply without a code redeploy.
Before the next deploy, reconcile that change into project source or explicitly choose the Hub copy when conflict handling appears.

flows.name: 42 — Replay a traced generation in Playground
steps: Select a generation inside a trace.
Add to → Playground → Fresh playground.
The Playground receives generation messages and model settings.
Submit to rerun, edit and compare outputs.

flows.name: 47 — Run full-application experiments and CI regression gates
steps: Implement a Python or JavaScript task and item/run evaluators using the experiment SDK.
Use hosted or local data, pin dataset version where needed and configure concurrency.
Run in CI; raise RegressionError when policy thresholds or approved-case checks fail.
Configure langfuse/experiment-action to publish results/PR comments and fail the job.
Optionally configure a signed remote trigger so the UI can start an external SDK experiment.

flows.name: Opik — run the actual agent with unsaved prompt overrides
steps: Mark the agent entrypoint with the SDK and load Prompt Library prompts inside it.
Start opik endpoint --project … -- python3 my_agent.py and keep the process alive.
Pair with the browser and open the connected Agent Playground.
Fill generated parameter inputs and Run; inspect the result/full live trace.
Edit a prompt or choose another version in the Prompts panel; rerun using unsaved overrides.
Save a satisfactory edit as a new prompt version.

flows.name: Tessl — generate or author scenarios, including repository-history tasks
steps: Create/link a Tessl project and ensure Publisher access.
Run tessl scenario generate on a plugin, optionally choosing a target count.
Wait or inspect the generation ID; download it to that plugin's evals directory.
Review/edit task.md, criteria.json and optional scenario.json, or write those files manually.
Alternatively generate from repository commits or PRs after connecting GitHub/GitLab.
Match runtime context globs to the context stripped from the fixture; bound commit fixture includes.

flows.name: Tessl — compare with-skill and without-skill outcomes
steps: Prepare reviewed scenarios in the plugin's evals directory.
Run tessl eval run on the plugin root.
By default Tessl solves each scenario with and without the context, with context activation forced in the with-context arm.
Score both arms against the same per-scenario rubric.
Inspect per-scenario outcomes as well as the average delta.
Repeat scenarios and rerun after edits to assess variability.

flows.name: Tessl — test activation and description boundaries
steps: Prepare positive, ambiguous and near-miss tasks.
Create description variants while keeping the body fixed.
Run with --skip-forced-context-activation and do not set agentMustRead.
Optionally add --skip-scoring for activation-only evaluation.
Inspect the transcript-derived activation evidence and per-solution records.
For the Claude agent Tessl counts Skill-tool events; other agents currently report activation as not measured.

flows.name: Tessl — compare models, agents, rewrites and ablations
steps: List available agents/models and prepare the same scenarios and judge.
Declare uniquely labeled configurations with --variant-json.
Vary only the model for model comparisons, or disclose combined agent/model changes when a common model is unavailable.
Swap the context fixture to compare rewrites; set context to null for a no-skill baseline.
Add codebase fixtures for neither/source-only/skill-only/both comparisons.
Prepare reduced plugin directories for leave-one-skill-out ablations; repeat and inspect score, variability, cost, time, tokens and turns.

flows.name: Tessl — monitor, compare, retry and gate asynchronous evaluations
steps: Submit an eval and retain its run ID.
In an interactive terminal the CLI waits; in CI/piped/JSON mode it normally submits and exits.
Use --wait and optionally --wait-timeout for terminal-result gating.
If waiting expires or Ctrl+C detaches, inspect the same server-side run rather than assuming cancellation.
Use eval list/view, --full statistics and eval compare for separate runs.
Use eval retry for failed runs; review resulting evidence before release.

flows.name: 10. Link an existing skill repository into an agent
steps: Choose a skill repository to reuse.
Author a files entry at a path such as skills/research with type skill and repo_handle.
Choose a current selector or omit it for LATEST, then create the parent commit.
Read the parent directory to inspect the linked repository and resolved commit.
These steps are documented through SDK/REST; an exact Context Hub UI Add linked skill picker sequence is not documented in the reviewed material.

flows.name: 11. Link another agent repository as a subagent
steps: Choose another agent repository.
Create an entry such as agents/scheduler with type agent and repo_handle.
Select LATEST or COMMIT using the directory API contract and commit the parent.
Inspect the resolved linked agent through directory reads.
The official screenshot shows a collapsed subagents tree node, but it does not expose a link-creation or selector dialog.

flows.name: 12. Choose pinned versus latest dependencies and handle upstream propagation
steps: For a linked agent/skill, author selector {"type":"COMMIT","commit_id":"<uuid>"} to pin.
Use selector {"type":"LATEST"} or omit selector to follow latest.
Create the parent directory commit.
Read the directory response to inspect the authored selector plus resolved owner, repository handle and commit hash.

The concepts/SDK guide says linked updates propagate to referencing parents. The SDK prose suggests legacy commit_id pinning, but current REST explicitly says that legacy top-level field is accepted and ignored for selection, resolving as LATEST; selector and legacy commit_id are mutually exclusive.

flows.name: Compose shared skills and subagents with following links
steps: Publish reusable skill or agent repos.
In the parent files map add an entry such as skills/research with type skill and repo_handle, or agents/scheduler with type agent.
Omit selection or use REST selector {type:LATEST} for following behavior.
Commit the parent; the SDK guide says later linked-repo updates propagate to referencing parents.

flows.name: Pin linked dependencies and detect misleading legacy selectors
steps: Resolve the desired dependency commit UUID.
In current REST, write selector {type:COMMIT,commit_id:<uuid>} on the linked entry.
Read back the authored selector and resolved owner/repo_handle/commit_hash.
Do not rely on legacy top-level commit_id: the REST contract says it is accepted but ignored for selection and resolves as LATEST; it cannot coexist with selector.

flows.name: Agenta — publish once, reuse across agents, pin or follow latest
steps: Open project Skills and create or import a skill.
Publish the skill.
Open each agent's Skills section and add the stored skill.
Choose an exact revision or Latest; API configurations may use @ag.embed references.
When a pinned reference shows Update available, re-add it pinned to the new version or switch to Latest.
For repository imports, choose Check for updates in the skill menu.

flows.name: Refresh checkpointed skill metadata after changes
steps: With a checkpointer, Deep Agents stores skills_metadata once per thread.
For deepagents>=0.7.16, pass skills_metadata=None in the next run input or call update_state with that value.
Do not use an empty list: that means discovery completed with no skills.
A middleware reset should happen in after_agent, not after_model; loading occurs at the next run start.
Changed discovery metadata changes the system prompt and invalidates its prompt cache.

flows.name: Force a selected skill into a run with pinned_skills
steps: For deepagents>=0.7.23, pass skill names in pinned_skills with run input.
Middleware reads each named SKILL.md and appends its body, without frontmatter, as a HumanMessage in the specified order.
The app may parse slash references or menu selection and pass the names; Deep Agents does not parse message syntax itself.
Unknown or unreadable skills are skipped with debug logging.
Pinned messages remain unchanged; repinning appends current text and makes associated skill tools available.

flows.name: Diagnose discovered, activated, delivered and successful skill behavior
steps: Use LangSmith traces to inspect discovery, read_file calls on SKILL.md and supporting-resource access.
For missing startup skills, check backend paths, parent source level, frontmatter, the 10 MB discovery skip and source shadowing.
For nonactivation, improve descriptions, reduce overlap, verify source configuration or explicitly pin the skill.
For missing resources/tools, inspect references, sandbox transfer, include_tools formatting/names and summarization state.
For stale skills, reset checkpointed metadata; for custom subagents, configure their sources explicitly.

flows.name: Verify adoption after a release or rollback rather than assuming it
steps: Move the production/staging tag to the intended commit.
Applications resolving that tag can subsequently pull the selected context; exact pins do not move.
Disk installations require another pull; persistent Deep Agents threads may require metadata refresh.
Inspect runtime traces/receipts to determine the context actually used rather than treating tag movement as delivery.

flows.name: 46 — Compare experiment runs and hand evidence to reviewers
steps: Open Experiments and select comparable runs.
Choose the reviewed release run as baseline; use the same dataset version and evaluator definitions.
Filter by score thresholds, inspect outputs and open traces for regressions.
Send reviewers run links, baseline/candidate identities, filters and release policy.
Maintain the approved baseline artifact and gate policy separately in the repository.

flows.name: PromptLayer — release labels and protected approval requests
steps: Open a prompt version and add a release label.
Retrieve the intended version with label in the SDK/run call.
For protected labels, request the label change rather than treating ordinary author access as promotion authority.
An authorized approval or denial resolves the pending change.
Observe requested/approved/denied events through documented webhook types.
Exact protected-label configuration/approval-button placement was not established from the retrieved pages; no click path is invented.

flows.name: 22. Promote to production with a defensible release decision
steps: Select the target commit.
Click Promote → Promote to Production.
The production tag moves to the selected commit.
Runtimes resolving :production subsequently pull that commit.
The core Context Hub guide does not document an integrated candidate/baseline evidence review, mandatory evaluation gate or approval inbox.

flows.name: Tessl — CI review/publish and multi-repository rollout
steps: Configure setup-tessl in a GitHub Actions workflow.
Create a workspace API key and store it as the repository TESSL_TOKEN secret.
Run review with explicit workspace, JSON output and threshold to fail CI below the configured bar.
For distribution, open the workspace plugin and click Rollout.
Choose destination workspace/repositories and Create a rollout PR.
Review and merge generated dependency changes through the repository's own process.

flows.name: 23. Roll an environment back to a historical commit
steps: Select the prior commit in history.
Choose Promote → Staging or Production.
The environment tag moves to the historical commit.
Latest files do not change and no revert commit is created.
The screenshot's curved-arrow control is visible, but the Context Hub guide does not describe its separate dialog; the documented rollback path is historical promotion.

flows.name: 14 — Roll back and verify post-rollback consumption
steps: Select the earlier good version and move production back to it.
API clients receive the new target on subsequent manifest retrieval, subject to application caching.
Run langfuse skills update for local installations following labels.
Exact version pins stay fixed; inspect traces/Usage to see observed versions.

flows.name: 16 — Review a skill's Usage tab
steps: Open a particular skill version → Usage.
Choose a date range containing the relevant runs.
Read Available and Loaded observation counts and per-file loads.
Filter Any/Available/Loaded, click a file to filter matching loads, then open a linked observation.

flows.name: 17 — Report available skills through Python, JavaScript or raw OpenTelemetry
steps: Configure tracing before agent observations start.
Raw OTel: set langfuse.observation.skills_available to a JSON string of name/version entries on each relevant span before it ends.
Python installed path: discover_skills, configure Langfuse skills.available, run inside propagate_attributes(attach_skills=True); fetched path supplies skills_available directly.
JavaScript installed path: await discoverSkills, configure LangfuseSpanProcessor, then propagateAttributes({attachSkills:true}); fetched path supplies skillsAvailable.
Flush/shutdown the exporter for a short-lived process.

flows.name: 18 — Instrument actual skill and supporting-file loads
steps: Attach available skills to the loading-tool observation.
Trace input/output using recognized tools: loadSkill/skill/Skill with name or skill; skill_read with skillName/path; readFile/Read with path/file_path containing the skill directory.
The tool must succeed and return non-null output to be recognized as a load.
For a different loader shape, the docs direct users to request support.

flows.name: 19 — Inspect available/requested/loaded context inside a trace
steps: Select a generation → Preview → Skills.
Expand available skills and follow saved-version links; inspect Requested/Not requested.
Select the associated successful loading tool → Preview → Skills.
Expand the loaded skill and file count to see paths; inspect the tool result to confirm load.

flows.name: 49 — Configure prompt caching and skill content reuse
steps: Use the high-level prompt SDK retrieval method.
Fresh cached prompts return immediately; expired entries are served while background revalidation runs.
Adjust the default 60-second TTL, or use TTL 0 for uncached fetches.
For skills, cache content by hash yourself or use locally installed files; SDK skill fetches are not automatically cached.

flows.name: 50 — Prewarm prompts and use explicit offline fallback
steps: Prefetch prompts at startup and fail readiness if required prompts cannot be loaded.
Alternatively supply a text/chat fallback to the SDK retrieval method.
Inspect is_fallback/isFallback to distinguish fallback execution.
Without fresh/stale cache or fallback, a failed first fetch raises an error.
